1. Project Vision & The "Zero-Identity-Swapping" Mandate

Biometric Hair AI is an enterprise-grade biometric hairstyling and cephalometric recommendation system built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. Traditional generative makeover applications (such as FaceApp, Lensa, and generic Stable Diffusion / ControlNet pipelines) suffer from an unacceptable clinical flaw: "Identity Drift". In generating a new hairstyle, existing models alter the user's bone structure, reconstruct their facial thirds, smooth away distinctive features, modify ethnic skin pigmentation, and replace the user's authentic facial identity with a synthetic stranger.

The Core Anthropometric Thesis
Hairstyles should not be applied as cosmetic filters. A haircut is a volumetric compensatory architectural counterweight designed to balance neoclassical cephalometric proportions:
  • Neoclassical Farkas Facial Thirds: The canonical facial profile divides into three equal 33.3% segments: Upper (Trichion hairline to Glabella brow line), Middle (Glabella to Subnasale nose base), and Lower (Subnasale to Gnathion chin tip).
  • Facial Index (Morphological Breadth): Measured as (Morphological Facial Height / Bizygomatic Breadth) × 100.
  • Golden Ratio Harmony (φ = 1.618): Scoring the deviation between facial width and longitudinal cranial balance.

Our mandate requires Zero-Identity-Swapping: The user's face (forehead, brows, eyes, glasses, nose, cheekbones, lips, jaw, and chin) must remain 100% bit-for-bit mathematically immutable, while the hairstyle is dynamically composited, volumetrically scaled, and shaded to sit seamlessly on the cranial vault.

4. Critical Engineering Hurdles, Lingering Failures & Bug Forensics

This section documents the exact technical challenges, mathematical discrepancies, and stubborn bugs encountered during implementation. This is the core diagnostic data required for Claude's advisory review.

4.1 The "Floating Toupee" Mid-Air Hair Displacement Bug

Symptom: In production testing, after capturing a portrait, the synthesized hairstyle (e.g. Textured French Crop) was rendered 150–200 pixels above the user's head, hovering like a detached wig in the empty white background above the cranium.

Figure 4A: Visual Evidence of the "Floating Toupee" Bug
The hair asset is rendered at Y ≈ 10% of the canvas height, while the user's actual forehead sits at Y ≈ 36%.
Forensic Root Cause Analysis:
  1. Shirtless/Chest Skin Pixel Accumulation: The user was shirtless. The YCbCr skin detector summed all skin pixels across the frame. Torso skin dominated the count, dragging the centroid down to the neck, inflating calculated faceHeight to >65% of the frame.
  2. Hairline Clamp Saturation: Subtracting faceHeight * 0.25 drove finalHairlineY below zero, saturated by Math.max(12, ...) at 12%.
  3. Synthetic Landmark Glabella Collapse: In fallback mode, Landmark 151 (Glabella) was set to finalHairlineY (same as Landmark 10), reducing foreheadH to a min clamp of 18px.
  4. PNG Bounding Box Discrepancy: In the 1024×1024 asset, content only spans Y=123 to Y=776. The draw call placed the image center at posY = targetBottomY - hairHeight * 0.25, floating the hair into the sky.
Status: Partially mitigated via cranial row-scanner; needs robust neural anchoring.
Figure 4B: Technical Root Cause Breakdown
Mathematical chain of failure leading to the displacement.

4.2 WebGL PerspectiveCamera vs. 2D object-fit: cover Unprojection Mismatch

Symptom: In the original 3D WebGL camera implementation, 3D GLB hair models and the biometric tracking oval were rendered far in the upper-right corner of the screen against the empty wall, completely detached from the user's face.

Figure 5: Aspect-Ratio Unprojection Skewing World Space
MediaPipe landmarks on raw video (640×480, 4:3) mapped into a tall mobile container (9:19.5) without letterbox compensation.
The Mathematical Mismatch Equation:

MediaPipe WASM outputs normalized coordinates (x, y) ∈ [0, 1] relative to the raw video hardware frame (aspect R_vid = W_vid / H_vid).

The UI renders the video with CSS object-fit: cover inside container (W_cont, H_cont) with aspect R_cont = W_cont / H_cont.

If R_cont > R_vid ⇒ Cropped Top/Bottom: OffsetY = (H_cont - W_cont / R_vid) / 2
If R_cont < R_vid ⇒ Cropped Left/Right: OffsetX = (W_cont - H_cont × R_vid) / 2

Because Three.js NDC space [-1, 1] did not apply this crop transformation, the camera projected landmarks into outer space. This led to our pivot from 3D WebGL to 2D landmark canvas tracking.

Figure 6: Aspect Ratio Normalization Mathematics
Formula required to reconcile hardware stream and screen pixels.

4.3 Background Silhouette Inpainting & Short Haircut Bleed

The Problem: When a user with existing long, voluminous, or wavy hair selects a short hairstyle (e.g. Textured French Crop, Buzz Fade, Taper Fade), their original hair protrudes significantly outside the boundary of the new haircut.

  • Current Implementation: photorealisticHairSynthesis.ts attempts an ambient background tone sampling pass in the upper corners and blurs dark non-skin pixels outside the target haircut perimeter.
  • Why It Fails: Simple luminance and chrominance heuristics cannot reconstruct complex non-uniform backgrounds (e.g., brick walls, door frames, wallpaper patterns, dynamic shadows). It leaves blurry smudges or accidentally clips into the ears and neck.

4.4 Metro Bundler SSR Crashes: Requiring unknown module "59"

The Problem: During rapid code iteration on React Native Web, Metro bundler intermittently crashes with Server Error: Requiring unknown module "59" inside /expo-server/build/cjs/vendor/abstract... at const html = await getHtml(request, ...).

  • Root Cause: In app.json, setting "web": { "output": "server" } triggers server-side rendering in Node.js. When client components import browser-specific APIs (window, document, AudioContext, Canvas) or when modules are deleted while Metro is running, Metro's SSR module graph desynchronizes.
  • Resolution Applied: Switched app.json to "output": "single" (SPA mode) and cleared cache (npx expo start -c). However, dynamic imports in Expo Web continue to present caching vulnerabilities.

4.5 Hair Strand Translucency & Hard Face Mask Seams

The Problem: The zero-identity-swapping mandate uses createFaceOvalPath with globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out' to subtract the protected facial polygon.

  • While this guarantees the face is 100% untouched, it creates an unnatural hard vector scissor cut across the upper forehead where bangs and hair strands drape over the skin. Real hair has individual translucent strands and micro-contact shadows that require soft alpha feathering.

5. Specific Architectural & Algorithmic Prompts for Claude

Please review the following targeted technical questions and provide concrete, production-grade solutions:

Question 1: Robust Anatomical Head Localizer Immune to Torso / Shirtless Skin

When client-side MediaPipe FaceMesh is initializing or throttled, our fallback YCbCr skin detector gets corrupted by exposed shoulders and chest. How can we write a fast, lightweight, pure JavaScript / Canvas algorithm (executing in <5ms) that robustly isolates the human cranium and forehead from the neck and torso, regardless of clothing?

Question 2: Universal Aspect Ratio Matrix for object-fit: cover to Canvas

What is the mathematically rigorous affine transform matrix to map normalized landmarks (u, v) ∈ [0, 1] from a camera stream of arbitrary aspect ratio (e.g. 4:3 or 16:9) to an interactive canvas inside a container rendered with object-fit: cover (e.g. 9:19.5), accounting for mirroring and devicePixelRatio without clipping?

Question 3: Realistic Background Inpainting for Original Silhouette Suppression

When replacing long hair with a short crop, how can client-side canvas logic cleanly erase the original hair silhouette that extends outside the new haircut envelope without turning the background into a blurry smudge? What generative or algorithmic patch-match inpainting approach works best client-side?

Question 4: Soft-Mask Alpha Feathering for Zero-Identity-Swapping Forehead Draping

How can we implement a dual-pass shader or 2D canvas composite operation that preserves 100% of facial features (brows, eyes, nose, glasses) while allowing semi-transparent hair fringe strands to cast soft contact shadows and drape naturally over the upper third of the forehead?

Question 5: Seamless Offline Bundling of MediaPipe 468 Face Mesh in Expo Web

Currently, injecting https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/.../face_mesh.js via script tags is vulnerable to network latency and adblockers, but importing @mediapipe/face_mesh or @mediapipe/tasks-vision directly causes Metro bundling errors on Web. What is the clean, official architecture to bundle MediaPipe WASM assets locally inside an Expo Router web project?
